reasoning.content: Open Repository → Contributors, preserve the current URL’s origin and full project namespace, and replace only the ref segment in the contributors route; an omitted search result does not justify guessing another host or namespace, and Repository → Graph is a different view. Confirm the “Commits to …” heading names the requested branch, compare every contributor’s displayed commit total and include all ties, then open each qualifying contributor’s profile and copy the complete visible follower count—never infer it from the contributor row, an abbreviated identity, or a near-matching profile.

reasoning.title: Preserve origin and verify the requested ref
reasoning.description: Use when a repository question depends on a specific branch and then requires profile data; do not use the currently displayed branch or a similarly named ref without verification.
reasoning.content: Open Repository → Contributors, use the visible branch selector, and if the requested ref is not selectable, construct a complete absolute URL from the current page’s exact origin, namespace, project path, and contributors route—never invent a host or rewrite the namespace. Confirm the heading names the requested ref, compare every contributor count and retain all ties, then open the exact matching contributor profile and copy the full visible Followers value rather than inferring it from the report or a near-identical identity.

reasoning.title: Preserve the project URL when changing contributor branches
reasoning.description: Use when GitLab’s Repository → Contributors report opens on the wrong branch or the requested branch is missing from the “Switch branch/tag” list; do not switch hosts, namespaces, or use the separate Repository → Graph view.
reasoning.content: Keep the current scheme, host, port, namespace, project, and `/-/graphs/` route unchanged, replacing only the final branch segment, then verify the “Commits to …” heading names the requested branch. Compare every contributor row and retain all ties for the highest commit count; open each linked profile and copy the complete visible “Followers” value, never guessing from a name, email, abbreviated row, or similar account.
